title: tervez vs. fog: Planning vs. Predicting

sections.title: A plan you're making vs. a statement about the future
sections.content: tervez + infinitive means you're actively deciding, arranging, working something out — a real plan taking shape, even if the details aren't fixed yet. fog + infinitive is more general: a prediction, an intention, or a promise, without necessarily meaning you've sat down and planned anything. If someone could reasonably ask "Oh, what's the plan?" and expect real details back, reach for tervez. If you're just saying what you expect or intend to happen, fog is the natural choice.

items.english: What are you planning in your career? (a real, thought-out plan)
I'm planning to look for a new job. (an active decision)

items.spanish: Biztosan sokat fogok tanulni ebben az állásban.
items.english: I'll definitely learn a lot in this job. (a prediction, not a plan itself)

items.spanish: Esetleg gondolkodom egy előléptetésen, de még nem tervezek semmit.
items.english: I'm possibly thinking about a promotion, but I'm not planning anything yet.

sections.content: Notice the last example: gondolkodik ("to think about, consider") on its own doesn't commit to anything — it's even weaker than fog. tervez is the strongest of the three: it means the decision is actually being made.
